payload.task_text:
You are a business development manager for TechStore Online, an e-commerce company selling consumer electronics and accessories. Your task is to plan a product roadshow in Shanghai and Guangzhou to meet regional distributors, selecting the right products to demonstrate based on store sales data, arranging train travel from Beijing, building a comprehensive roadshow plan spreadsheet, documenting the plan in the company knowledge base, and notifying all key contacts.

Start by analyzing the online store data. Retrieve the top ten products by sales volume from the product sales report. For each of the top five products, get the full product details including name, price, category, and stock status. Then retrieve the customer list and examine the billing location information to understand regional customer distribution. Also pull the orders report to understand regional revenue patterns. Per the company's strategic direction, the roadshow will focus on Shanghai and Guangzhou; use the customer and orders analysis to prepare the regional overview and mark Shanghai and Guangzhou as Priority 1 in the plan.

Next, plan the train travel. Look up the station codes for Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou using the train booking system. Query available high-speed trains from Beijing South station to Shanghai Hongqiao station on March 10, 2026, and from Beijing South to Guangzhou South on the same day. Review the options for each leg and pick one suitable for arriving in time for the afternoon meetings. The roadshow configuration file in your workspace lists the preferred trains for both legs; use those selections so the itinerary aligns with the company's standing travel preferences.

Create an Excel workbook named Roadshow_Plan.xlsx in your workspace. It must contain four sheets. The first sheet should be named Products and contain columns: Product_ID, Name, Category, Price_USD, Stock_Status, and Monthly_Sales_Est. Populate it with the five products selected for demonstration. The second sheet should be named Customer_Regions and contain columns: Region, Customer_Count, Revenue_Share_Pct, and Priority. Add rows for the key regions identified in the customer data analysis, marking Shanghai and Guangzhou as Priority 1. The third sheet should be named Travel_Itinerary and contain columns: Date, Train_No, From, To, Depart, Arrive, Duration_Hours, and Purpose. Add a row for the journey to Shanghai on March 10 and a row for the journey to Guangzhou. The fourth sheet should be named Roadshow_Schedule and contain columns: City, Date, Venue, Meeting_Type, Key_Contacts, and Status. Add at least four rows covering the Shanghai meeting on March 10 and the Guangzhou meeting on March 11. Write all numeric values (prices, counts, percentages, durations) as literal numbers in the cells; do not use spreadsheet formulas.

Create a page in the company knowledge base titled "Product Roadshow 2026 - Shanghai and Guangzhou". Add a section highlighting the five demonstration products with key selling points for each. Add a travel itinerary section showing both train journeys with departure and arrival details. Add a checklist section called "Follow-up Actions" listing items such as sending product catalogs to distributors, collecting distributor feedback forms, and scheduling follow-up calls.

Send an email to shanghai_dist@partner.com with subject "Roadshow Meeting Confirmation - Shanghai March 10" providing full details of the planned meeting time, venue, and products to be demonstrated. Send a second email to guangzhou_dist@partner.com with subject "Roadshow Meeting Confirmation - Guangzhou March 11" with the Guangzhou meeting details and a list of products. Send a summary email to manager@company.com with subject "Roadshow Plan Summary - Shanghai and Guangzhou March 2026" attaching a brief overview of the itinerary, the five products selected, and the expected business outcomes.

Configuration for this task is in roadshow_config.json and the planning methodology guide is in business_guide.md, both in your workspace.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use exactly one read-only source wave. Before dispatch, the main agent reads `roadshow_config.json` and `business_guide.md` and freezes the preferred train displays, two-city schedule, three exact email pairs, and output schemas.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 explore sub-agents in parallel:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): The WooCommerce explore sub-agent calls `woo_reports_top_sellers` once, retrieves the exact top-five products by ID with one `woo_products_get` call per ID, and fully paginates only `woo_customers_list` and `woo_orders_list` at `perPage=100`. Omit the optional order status field to request the unfiltered collection, aggregate every observed status locally, and return only the five product rows plus compact Shanghai/Guangzhou customer-count, order-revenue, share, page, and join controls. Do not write files or modify the store.
   2. explore 1 (web-domain-researcher 0): The rail explore sub-agent resolves Beijing South, Shanghai Hongqiao, and Guangzhou South codes, queries both 2026-03-10 high-speed routes, and returns the exact task-configured preferred trains with display train number, route identifier where required, departure, arrival, duration, and first-class evidence. Do not write files.

After Wave 1, the main agent validates the two compact handoffs once and directly owns all outputs. Create `Roadshow_Plan.xlsx` with exactly the four required sheets, five products, both configured train rows, and at least four city schedule rows using literal numeric values. In an independent branch, exact-title search and create/update at most one `Product Roadshow 2026 - Shanghai and Guangzhou` page with the five product selling points, both train legs, and `Follow-up Actions`. Read the workbook and page once, then send at most one missing message for each of the three exact recipient/subject pairs. Do not dispatch a writer or verification wave.

nodes.text:
Develop an execution and validation plan for this multi-system roadshow task. Read only the workspace inputs /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-12306-wc-amazon-product-roadshow-excel-notion/workspace/roadshow_config.json and business_guide.md, and identify required data fields, likely ambiguities (especially two journeys both originating Beijing on Mar 10), sequencing, and acceptance checks. You may inspect read-only WooCommerce/rail metadata if useful, but do not mutate anything. Return concise findings including exact preferred trains/config values and planning methodology requirements. Do not create artifacts.
Plan roadshow workflow

Read these exact workspace files and return their contents in a concise structured summary, without modifying anything: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-12306-wc-amazon-product-roadshow-excel-notion/workspace/roadshow_config.json and /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-12306-wc-amazon-product-roadshow-excel-notion/workspace/business_guide.md. Extract all preferred train numbers, dates, station pairs, meeting times/venues/contacts, WooCommerce analysis periods or assumptions, regional grouping rules, product selection/ranking rules, expected outcomes, and Notion parent/page configuration if present. Acceptance: exact values and note any unspecified fields. Do not create files.
Inspect roadshow inputs

Analyze WooCommerce store data for TechStore Online roadshow planning. Requirements: (1) retrieve the top ten products by sales volume from the product sales report, paginating if needed; (2) for the top five by total sales volume, fetch full product details and report product ID, name, category name/ID, regular/current price in USD, stock status/quantity, total sales and a defensible literal Monthly_Sales_Est (use total sales as estimate only if no analysis period exists, clearly state method); (3) retrieve the full customer list (paginate, up to all available) and examine billing city/state/country; (4) retrieve enough orders/customer or order reports to estimate regional revenue patterns, grouping by billing city/state and calculating customer counts and revenue shares for key regions. The guide says Priority 1 >20%, Priority 2 10–20%, but regardless Shanghai and Guangzhou must be Priority 1 strategically. No explicit date range exists, so use all available/current report data and disclose. Return a concise canonical dataset suitable for Excel plus evidence/assumptions. Read-only only; do not mutate store data.
Analyze store roadshow data

Use the 12306 tools to plan and verify two high-speed rail journeys on 2026-03-10: Beijing South to Shanghai Hongqiao, and Beijing South to Guangzhou South. First resolve station codes through the station-name lookup tool (do not guess codes), then query available G trains for each route and review options suitable for afternoon/next-morning meetings. The authoritative preferences are G11 for Shanghai (configured 07:00–12:31, first class) and G105 for Guangzhou (configured 08:00–15:48, first class). Select those preferred trains if returned and report exact ticket result fields, depart/arrive times, duration hours as a literal decimal, and availability. If live results differ or preferred trains are absent, explicitly say so and retain configured preferred itinerary as standing preference. Also note feasibility: these are separate alternative outbound legs for roadshow planning and cannot be taken by one traveler simultaneously; however user explicitly requires both rows. Read-only, no booking.
Select preferred rail options

Create and verify the Excel workbook at /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-12306-wc-amazon-product-roadshow-excel-notion/workspace/Roadshow_Plan.xlsx. Use only Excel/local artifact tools and keep all content inside workspace. Exactly four sheets named and structured as follows; numeric values must be literal numbers, never formulas.

1) Products columns: Product_ID, Name, Category, Price_USD, Stock_Status, Monthly_Sales_Est. Rows:
10 | NIHARA Wood Smart Multipurpose Foldable Laptop Table with Cup Holder Ergonomic & Rounded Edges (Black) | Electronics | 2.64 | In stock (11) | 199
74 | (Renewed) JBL Flip 4 Portable Wireless Speaker with Powerful Bass & Mic (Squad) | Audio; Speakers | 86.72 | In stock (8) | 198
68 | LIMBANI BROTHERS™ Automatic Vacuum Sealing Machine for Flatbreads, Nuts, Vegetables, Fruits and Dry Fruits | Home Appliances | 12.04 | In stock (21) | 197
9 | Oraimo 25.5W 4 Ports USB Charger, 5.1A USB Wall Charger Phone Adapter | Electronics | 7.22 | In stock (20) | 195
44 | Oppo Enco Air 3 True Wireless in-Ear Earbuds, 25hrs Playtime, Fast Charging, 13.4mm Driver, BT v5.3 | Audio; Headphones | 36.13 | In stock (16) | 195
(Current sale price is used.)

2) Customer_Regions columns: Region, Customer_Count, Revenue_Share_Pct, Priority. Rows use city-only grouping of customer lifetime spend: Shanghai | 0 | 0 | Priority 1 - Strategic; Guangzhou | 0 | 0 | Priority 1 - Strategic; Phoenix | 5 | 12.61 | Priority 2; San Jose | 2 | 11.94 | Priority 2; Columbus | 7 | 10.41 | Priority 2; San Diego | 4 | 6.63 | Monitor; Dallas | 3 | 6.84 | Monitor. Keep Shanghai/Guangzhou first. (All source customers are US; these two are strategic overrides.)

3) Travel_Itinerary columns: Date, Train_No, From, To, Depart, Arrive, Duration_Hours, Purpose. Rows: 2026-03-10 | G11 | Beijing South | Shanghai Hongqiao | 07:00 | 12:31 | 5.5167 | Shanghai distributor meeting and product demonstration; 2026-03-10 | G105 | Beijing South | Guangzhou South | 08:00 | 15:48 | 7.8 | Guangzhou distributor meeting next morning. These are separate alternative outbound legs explicitly required; preserve both.

4) Roadshow_Schedule columns: City, Date, Venue, Meeting_Type, Key_Contacts, Status. Add these rows: Shanghai | 2026-03-10 14:00-16:00 | Shanghai Distributor Office (address TBC) | Portfolio overview and live product demonstration | shanghai_dist@partner.com | Planned; Guangzhou | 2026-03-11 09:00-10:00 | Guangzhou Distributor Office (address TBC) | Company and product portfolio overview | guangzhou_dist@partner.com | Planned; Guangzhou | 2026-03-11 10:00-12:00 | same venue | Live demonstration of five products | same contact | Planned; Guangzhou | 2026-03-11 12:00-13:00 | same venue | Business lunch with distributor management | same contact | Planned; Guangzhou | 2026-03-11 13:00-15:00 | same venue | Commercial negotiation and terms discussion | same contact | Planned; Guangzhou | 2026-03-11 15:00-16:00 | same venue | Facility tour and logistics review | same contact | Planned.

Apply professional formatting: bold colored headers, frozen header rows if supported, widths/wrap text, price/percent/duration sensible number formats, Excel tables on each dataset, dates/times displayed clearly. Do not add extra sheets. Verify by re-reading metadata and all populated ranges; return exact artifact path and verification summary.
Build roadshow workbook

Create a Notion company knowledge-base page titled exactly "Product Roadshow 2026 - Shanghai and Guangzhou". No parent is specified, so first search Notion for a plausible company knowledge-base/home/team page; choose the best existing accessible page as parent. If none exists, create at workspace root if API permits. The page must clearly include:
- Executive/regional overview: store report 128 orders and $50,777.88 gross sales; customer geography sample 50 registered customers, all currently US; Shanghai and Guangzhou are Priority 1 strategic expansion markets despite 0 observed current customers/revenue; Phoenix, San Jose, Columbus are Priority 2 by city-only customer-spend share.
- Section "Demonstration Products" with five products and key selling points:
1. NIHARA foldable laptop table — portable ergonomic design, cup holder, strong volume leader.
2. Renewed JBL Flip 4 portable wireless speaker — powerful bass, microphone, portable proven audio demand.
3. LIMBANI BROTHERS automatic vacuum sealing machine — versatile food preservation across flatbreads, nuts, produce and dry fruits.
4. Oraimo 25.5W four-port USB charger — multi-device 5.1A charging and broad smartphone compatibility.
5. Oppo Enco Air 3 true wireless earbuds — 25-hour playtime, fast charging, 13.4mm drivers, Bluetooth 5.3.
Mention selected on sales volume (199,198,197,195,195 cumulative units respectively).
- Section "Travel Itinerary" with both: Mar 10 2026 G11 Beijing South 07:00 to Shanghai Hongqiao 12:31 (5h31m, first class available), purpose Shanghai 14:00 meeting; Mar 10 2026 G105 Beijing South 08:00 to Guangzhou South 15:48 (7h48m, first class available), purpose Guangzhou next-morning meeting. Add a prominent feasibility note that these are overlapping alternative outbound legs and require separate travelers or a revised sequential itinerary; one traveler cannot take both.
- Section "Roadshow Schedule": Shanghai Mar 10 14:00–16:00 at Shanghai Distributor Office (address TBC), demonstration/overview, contact shanghai_dist@partner.com. Guangzhou Mar 11 09:00–16:00 at Guangzhou Distributor Office (address TBC), overview, demos, lunch, negotiation, facility/logistics review, contact guangzhou_dist@partner.com.
- Checklist section titled exactly "Follow-up Actions" with unchecked items including sending product catalogs/spec sheets to distributors, collecting distributor feedback forms, sending meeting notes and proposed terms within 48 hours, and scheduling follow-up calls two weeks after roadshow.
- Expected outcomes: validate distributor demand, negotiate commercial terms, assess logistics readiness, build prioritized follow-up pipeline.
Use headings, bullets, and to-do blocks professionally. Return page ID, title, parent chosen, and successful retrieval/verification details. External write is authorized.
Create roadshow Notion page

Send three authorized external emails for TechStore Online roadshow. Use professional plain-text bodies and send (not drafts). Product list in every relevant email: NIHARA foldable laptop table; Renewed JBL Flip 4 portable wireless speaker; LIMBANI BROTHERS automatic vacuum sealing machine; Oraimo 25.5W four-port USB charger; Oppo Enco Air 3 true wireless earbuds.

1) To shanghai_dist@partner.com, subject exactly "Roadshow Meeting Confirmation - Shanghai March 10". Confirm Tuesday March 10, 2026, 14:00–16:00 local time, venue "Shanghai Distributor Office (address TBC)", meeting includes portfolio overview and live demonstrations. Mention team planned arrival G11 Beijing South 07:00 -> Shanghai Hongqiao 12:31 and request/clearly state address confirmation is pending. Include all five products.

2) To guangzhou_dist@partner.com, subject exactly "Roadshow Meeting Confirmation - Guangzhou March 11". Confirm Wednesday March 11, 2026, 09:00–16:00 local time, venue "Guangzhou Distributor Office (address TBC)". Agenda: 09:00 overview, 10:00–12:00 demos, 12:00 lunch, 13:00–15:00 negotiations, 15:00–16:00 facility/logistics review. Include all five products. Mention planned reference itinerary G105 Mar 10 Beijing South 08:00 -> Guangzhou South 15:48 and request address confirmation.

3) To manager@company.com, subject exactly "Roadshow Plan Summary - Shanghai and Guangzhou March 2026". Include brief overview of both March 10 itineraries (G11 07:00–12:31 Shanghai; G105 08:00–15:48 Guangzhou), five selected products and cumulative sales units (199, 198, 197, 195, 195), regional finding (50 registered customers all US; Shanghai/Guangzhou Priority 1 strategic expansion), schedule, and expected outcomes: validate distributor demand, negotiate terms, assess logistics readiness, build follow-up pipeline. Explicitly flag that the two Mar 10 trains overlap and therefore require separate travelers or a revised sequential itinerary. Attach the existing workbook /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-12306-wc-amazon-product-roadshow-excel-notion/workspace/Roadshow_Plan.xlsx as the plan artifact (this satisfies and improves on the requested summary attachment). Verify successful send responses and return recipient, subject, message/send IDs, and attachment status. Do not send additional emails.
Send roadshow emails
